item.title: Antigravity Grounded! Security Vulnerabilities in Google's Latest IDE
item.description:
Author: wunderwuzzi
Date: November 25, 2025
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Software Development", "Artificial Intelligence", "Vulnerability Analysis"]
Summary:
  • Google released a new IDE called Antigravity last week.
  • It contains known security vulnerabilities from the Windsurf codebase.
  • Issues include remote command execution and data exfiltration.
  • Google started documenting these vulnerabilities publicly after reports.
  • Exploits bypass AI safety checks using indirect prompt injection.
  • The article raises awareness and suggests mitigations.

item.title: Indirect Prompt Injection: The Hidden Threat Breaking Modern AI Systems
item.description:
Author: Lakera Team
Date: November 24, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Prompt Injection", "Agentic AI", "Cybersecurity", "AI Safety"]
Summary:

item.title: The Embedded Threat in Your LLM: Poisoning RAG Pipelines via Vector Embeddings

Author: Nicolas Papernot
Date: N/A
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Adversarial Attacks", "Retrieval-Augmented Generation", "Vector Embeddings"]
Summary:

item.description:
Date: November 20, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Language Models", "Cybersecurity", "Adversarial Attacks"]

  • The method is called INPAINTING.
  • It turns prompt search into an efficient inference task.
  • The prompts bypass standard filters easily.

item.title: Manus Rubra: The Browser Extension With Its Hand in Everything Mindgard discovered that the Manus AI browser extension is for all intents and purposes, a full browser remote control backdoor.
item.description:
Author: Rich Smith
Date: November 18, 2025
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Browser Extensions", "Artificial Intelligence", "Privacy", "Software Risk Analysis"]
Summary:
  • Mindgard found Manus AI browser extension acts as a full remote control backdoor.
  • Manus AI aims to automate complex tasks across services.
  • The extension inherits all user sessions and bypasses access barriers.
  • It has high-risk permissions like debugger and cookies.
  • Over 40,000 users installed it within a week.
  • Experts warn this poses serious security risks.

item.title: Forced Descent: Google Antigravity Persistent Code Execution Vulnerability Mindgard identified a flaw in Google's Antigravity IDE that shows how traditional trust assumptions break down in AI-driven software.
item.description:

  • The flaw breaks traditional trust in AI software.
  • AI development environments need stricter security controls.

item.title: AI phishing attack in Australia: 270,000 fake government emails expose AI security gap
item.description:
Author: Giskard Team
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Phishing Attacks", "Artificial Intelligence", "Government Security", "Data Protection"]
Summary:
  • Australia faced an AI-driven phishing attack with 270,000 fake government emails.
  • The emails mimicked official agencies like the ATO.
  • Attackers used AI to create convincing phishing content at scale.
  • Traditional spam filters struggle to detect AI-generated phishing.
  • The ACSC issued warnings and guidelines to combat these threats.
  • This incident highlights the need for improved AI security measures.

item.title: Tree of attacks with pruning: The automated method for jailbreaking LLMs
item.description:
Author: Nicolas Papernot
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Machine Learning Security", "Natural Language Processing", "Cybersecurity", "Reinforcement Learning"]
Summary:
  • Large Language Models can be vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks.
  • The article presents a method called Tree of Attacks with Pruning (ToAP).
  • ToAP builds and prunes a tree of attack prompts to find jailbreaks.
  • It uses reinforcement learning and heuristics to improve efficiency.
  • Experiments show ToAP finds diverse and effective jailbreaks.
  • The method helps improve LLM safety and vulnerability understanding.
